The first respondent as complainant
filed a complaint before the District Forum against the opposite parties to
replace the goods with new goods of similar description from free from any
defect, to refund a sum of Rs.60,472/- being the repair charges, to pay Rs.1
lakh towards medical expenses, to pay Rs.1,60,000/- towards conveyance
expenses, during the break down of the vehicle, to pay Rs.10 lakhs being
compensation for hardships and mental agony, to pay Rs.6 lakhs towards
compensation for loss of reputation, career and income, to pay interest at 24%
on the total sum of Rs.19,20,472/- and to pay Rs.5,000/- towards cost. The District Forum partly allowed the
complaint. Against the said order, this
appeal is preferred by third opposite party, praying to set aside the order of
the District Forum dt.31.07.2006 in C.C.213/2005.
This
appeal coming before us for hearing finally on 24.11.2009. Upon hearing the arguments of the counsels on
eitherside, this commission made the following order:
Counsel for the
Appellants /1st & 2nd O.Ps. : Mr.Sathish
Parasaran, Advocate.
Counsel for the 1 Respdt/Complainant : Mrs.R. Maheswari,
Advocate.
Counsel for the 2nd Respdt/3rd O.P. :
Mr.K.V.Rajan, Advocate.
M. THANIKACHALAM J,
PRESIDENT
1. The third opposite party
in O.P.213/2005 is the appellant in F.A.591/2006 and first and second opposite
parties are the appellants in F.A.626/2006.
2. The first respondent, in
both the appeals, as complainant, approached the District Forum, Chennai
(South), complaining deficiency, against the opposite parties/appellants
seeking direction to replace the goods with new goods of similar description,
which shall be free from any defect, as well, for a recovery of total sum of
Rs.19,20,472/- on various heads on the following grounds (in brief).
3. The complainant purchased
Ford Ikon Rally Sport Car (Registration No.TN-01-D-0006) on 6.6.2000 for a sum
of Rs.6,16,286/- with one year warranty period, trusting the promise and
commitment made by the opposite parties.
Right from the date of purchase, the engine of the car in question
developed frequent problems, by abnormal jerking with heavy noise thereby
causing the complainant,, and others in the car, to feel scared and afraid of
traveling in the car, within the warranty period itself, necessitating
immediate repair and shelling out money from the pocket of the complainant in
view of the urgency and want of time.
4. The opposite parties did
not rectify the mistakes which resulted unnecessary expenses for the
complainant to travel elsewhere. With in
a few months of purchase, the manufacturing defect of the engine had manifested
itself by way of jerking of engine and engine noise, not rectified by the
second opposite party, who is an authorized service centre, though charged
excessively, collected a sum of Rs.60,472/-.
In view of the deficiency caused, legal notice was issued, for which, a
reply was given, wherein, the mistake was admitted by the opposite parties.
5. The opposite parties, in
order to repair the manufacturing defects, opened engine head and the said act,
instead of solving the problem, created leading to various other problems, such
as emitting black smoke, causing further noise.
Because of the repeated defects and the same was not rectified properly
by the second and third opposite parties, though the complainant had taken the
vehicle to them on various dates, they have committed deficiency in service to
the consumer, namely the complainant.
The first opposite party being the manufacturer is liable to replace the
vehicle and all the opposite parties are jointly and severally liable to pay
the above said sum also. Hence, the
complaint.
6. The first and second
opposite parties, denying all the allegations in the complaint, would contend
that the vehicle has run for around 36,646 kms from 6.6.2000 to 26.12.2004 and
the fact being so, the accusation of the complainant that there was
manufacturing defect in the engine is frivolous and untenable, that whenever
the vehicle was delivered for service/repairs, they were attended to the
satisfaction of the complainant, not challenged and therefore, there is no
deficiency of service, that when the complainant reported, engine vibrating at
idling, the same was rectified to the complainants satisfaction, that engine
noise and jerking cannot be due to manufacturing defect and it may be due to enormous
reasons including continuous use of the vehicle and wear and tear, for which, the
opposite parties cannot be held responsible, that the opposite parties never
admitted any manufacturing defect, at any point of time, that right from the
date of purchase, till 27.2.2003, no complaint was raised about the performance
of the engine which would be seen from the Job Cards from 27.2.2003 to
24.09.2004, wherein, the complainant also took the vehicle after satisfying
himself, that the complainant has been enjoying the comfort of the vehicle,
except some technical problem, that the complainant who delivered the vehicle
for repair, refused to take delivery of the vehicle despite being issued a
letter dated 27.01.2005 and even till this date, the complainant has not taken
delivery of the vehicle and that the complainant is taking unfair advantage of
a welfare legislation, claiming exorbitant amount and that since there is no
negligence or deficiency in service, no question of any damage could be granted
by these opposite parties, including punitive damages, thereby, prayed for the
dismissal of the case.
7. The third opposite party
in its separate Version, would contend that after 23.01.2003, the vehicle was
not serviced at their Station, that they have not committed any deficiency in
service or practiced any unfair trade practice, that all the averments are
frivolous, false and untenable, that the complainant is not entitled to any
relief, thereby, prayed for the dismissal of the complaint.
8. Based upon the pleadings,
the District Forum exhibiting 18 documents on the side of the complainant and 5
documents on the side of the opposite parties, evaluated the materials, framing
points for consideration also. After
evaluation and assessment of the evidence, the District Forum came to the
conclusion, that the defect in the engine was persisting continuously, the
second opposite party had not delivered the same, after making necessary
repairs, which should be construed as deficiency in service. It was further held that since the engine
head was opened to rectify the defects of jerking, the complainant is entitled to
replacement of the engine. In this view,
a direction came to be issued, directing all the opposite parties, to fix new
engine from any defect apart from repairing the vehicle, further directing the
opposite parties to pay a sum of Rs.25,000/- as compensation jointly and
severally, as per the order dated 31.07.2006, which is under challenge in both
the appeals.
9. The third opposite party
who is a Dealer/Service Station, not a manufacturer of the engine or the car,
as the case, may be, he cannot comply the direction. In this view, the third opposite party
aggrieved not only by the first direction, but also by the direction to pay the
compensation, questioning the findings, on various grounds filed separate
appeal in F.A.591/2006.
10. The first and second
opposite parties, one being the manufacturer, have also questioned the
reasonings given by the District Forum, not satisfied on various grounds, in
F.A.626/2005.
11. Heard the learned counsel
for the appellant, perusal of Written Arguments documents as well as the order
of the lower Forum.
12. The learned counsel,
appearing for the appellants in both the cases, would submit that in the
absence of proof regarding the manufacturing defect, the directions issued by
the lower forum, that too not following the procedure contemplated under
Section13 (b)
of Consumer Protection Act, is erroneous, liable to be set
aside. Further submission was made, on
behalf of the appellants, that after the warranty period was over, there is no
question of replacing the goods/engine, and in this case, the District Forum
without understanding the scope of the warranty, and the contract between the
parties, issued directions which are not within its jurisdiction and in this
view also, the order of the District Forum is to be eclipsed. Elaborating the above submissions, our
attention was also drawn to certain rulings, of the National Commission, where
it is held, the procedure contemplated under
Section 13 (b)
should be followed,
in this kind of cases.
13. Per contra, it is the
submission of the learned senior counsel representing the
complainant/respondent, that the defect, whether it is manufacturing or
otherwise, since Act does not contemplate manufacturing defect alone, existed
and persisted from the date of purchase of the vehicle and therefore, when that
was not rectified, the opposite parties are not entitled to escape from their
liability as if warranty period was over, whereas it should construed since the
defect occurred, even during the warranty period, still the same continuous, it
should further follow, as per the terms and conditions, the goods should be
replaced, in this case engine of the
car. Further submission of the learned
senior counsel was that because of the defects not repaired by the opposite parties, the complainant was put to hardship, mental agony, monetary
loss etc. and to redress the same, only a nominal amount was ordered as
compensation which cannot be faulted.
Supporting the above submission and to enlighten how the warranty should
be construed, our attention was also drawn to certain decisions of the Apex Court, as well as National Commission.
14. Hearing the submissions of
the learned counsel for the parties, perusing the records, then giving our
anxious thought, as well considering the date of purchase and the vehicle left
with the second opposite party for repair, we are of the considered opinion,
that the trial forum has not properly analyzed the case, applied the law
correctly, consequentially, delivered an erroneous order, which requires
setting aside, since in our further opinion, the complainant has not made out a
case, though in the lengthy complaint, he has described many things, which are
not germane to decide the point in issue.
15.
Section 2 (1) (f)
defines defect means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity,
potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any
law for the time being in force or [under any contract, express or implied, or]
as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods
and (g) defines deficiency means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming or inadequacy in the
quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by
or under any law for the time being in force has been undertaken to be
performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to
any service. While giving
meaning for goods, Act says, as defined in the
Sale of Goods Act, 1930
. Therefore, the warranty or condition defined
under the
Sale of Goods Act
, has to be taken into consideration, in this case,
in order to find out the defect or the deficiency as well the warranty.
16. As rightly submitted by
the learned senior counsel for the complainant/respondent, the Act nowhere says,
the defect should be manufacturing defect.
The defect contemplated under the
definition must be the manufacturing defect, inherent in nature or the defect
should have occurred, within the period of warranty because of the expression
used in (f) and (g) under any contract
, express or implied, undertaken to be
performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to
any service. Therefore, if the defect or the service
complained, had occurred or happened or not attended, was beyond the period of
warranty, which should be taken a contract or condition then, that kind of
activity cannot be brought in under the above said definition. True, if the defect was noticed, within the
period of warranty or if the deficiency had occurred within the period of
warranty, then continued, continuously or perpetually not corrected, then that can
be taken as covered under the contract or in pursuant of the contract, if there
is a failure to rectify the defect or if there is a deficiency in service.
17.
Section 13 (1)(c)
of the
Consumer Protection Act contemplates where the complainant alleges a defect in
the goods which cannot be determined, without proper analysis or test of the
goods, the District Forum shall obtain a sample of the goods from the
complainant, seal it and authenticate it in the manner prescribed and refer the
sample so sealed to the appropriate laboratory along with a direction that such
laboratory make analysis or test, whichever may be necessary, with a view to
finding out whether such goods suffer from any defect alleged in the complaint
or suffer from any other defect and to report its findings thereon to the
District Forum within a period of forty five days of the receipt of the
reference or within such extended period as may be granted by the District
Forum, which is mandatory in
nature, and this is also the dictum of National Commission, in several
decisions. In this case, admittedly, the
District Forum has not followed the procedure, in order to obtain a report,
about the defect alleged in the complaint regarding the car. In the absence of the expert opinion, based
upon the allegations in the complaint of the complainant alone, that too, after
4 years, deciding the case, car manufactured by the first opposite party was
defective, must be a defective decision, which is available here.
18. In the case decided in The Manager, Tata Engineering and
Locomotive Co. Ltd., Proprietor Commercial Motor, Dehradun and Proprietor
Commercial Motor, Rishikesh {II (2009) CPJ 190 (NC)}, a complaint came to
be lodged before the District Forum, that the manufacturer was guilty of supplying
a truck, with manufacturing defects to the purchaser, which was opposed and
despite on the strength of the warranty, a direction came to be issued, which
was finally under challenge before the National Commission, where the National
Commission has held, that when there is no reliable expert evidence to hold
that the truck suffered from any manufacturing defect, question of directing
the opposite party therein to refund the value of the vehicle is unjustified,
though the case was within the period of warranty. In the case on hand also, we do not have any
reliable expert evidence, since the District Forum has not obtained any report,
either on its own, on the basis of the allegation of the complainant or on the
petition filed by the complainant.
19. The National Commission in
LML Limited Vs.
Arun Kumar and Ors, in Para 7 of the order has noted that
both the lower Fora erred in not following the procedure laid down under
Section 13
of the CPA, which had to be done by us. The report of expert has been reproduced
earlier. Having perused the material on
record, and hearing the parties, we are quite clear that vehicle having run for
more than four years, it was not possible at this stage to arrive at a
conclusion about any manufacturing defect and repair cost of these defects
having placed at Rs.10,000. It is not in
dispute that the motorcycle was taken to O.Ps. 1 and 2 for repairs many times,
but only when nothing was done, a complaint was filed before the District
Forum, which decision is applicable to the present case.
Once again the National Commission in
Ajitha Chit Funds (P) Ltd., Vs.
Tata Engineering and Locomotive Co. Ltd., and Ors
, has held In the absence of evidence of expert to
that effect and car having diesel engine, it cannot be concludes as rightly
held by Fora below the car was having manufacturing defect. On the above basis, since there is no expert
opinion, except the bills and Job Cards, which we will discus hereunder, which
also not supportive of the complainants case, we conclude, that the
respondent/complainant has not made out a case of manufacturing defect or the
defect, as the case may be, from the day of purchase and therefore, at this
distance of time, direction to replace the engine may not be proper.
20. Admittedly, the
complainant purchased Ford Ikon Rally Sport Car from the opposite parties on
6.6.2000 for a sum of Rs.6,16,286/-. It
is also an admitted fact that the warranty period was one year and the case
came to be filed before the District Forum on 31.03.2005, that is 5 years after,
short of 3 months. The vehicle also run
36,646 kms as on 26.12.2004. Without
considering these things, after the warranty period was over, a direction came
to be issued, which appears to be not correct, that too, in view of the fact
that the complainant has not made out a case of manufacturing defect in the
engine within the period of warranty except small problem, which will arise ordinarily
in any mechanical device. If that
problem had not been set it right, within the period of warranty freely or
thereafter on payment basis, then only question of accusing the manufacturing
company or the service provider would arise which are also not available in
this case, which would be seen from the documents. Before going into documents, in order to find
out whether the complainant had established the defects, from the day one of
the purchase as claimed or atleast within the period of warranty as claimed, we
have to see certain decisions relied on by the learned senior counsel for the
respondent/complainant, to fit in with the case.
21. The Apex Court of India in
Jose Philip Mampillil Vs.
M/s.Premier Automobiles Ltd., & Another, reported in CDJ 2004 SC 281, though the condemned act and conduct of the
manufacturer or the dealer
in that case
, has not restored the order of the
District Forum, which directed replacement of the engine free of costs which
was upset by the State Commission, whereas gave direction to repair the
vehicle, pay damages etc., adding some more conditions, thereby, informing that
replacement of engine, alone was not the remedy. From
the facts available therein, it is clear even at the time of taking delivery,
the car was defective, since there were defects in the paints, and that the
piston rings of the engine had gone. In
spite of that, only compensation and repair alone was contemplated, and
question of replacement of the engine as directed by the District Forum not
restored.
22. The Apex Court in
Indochem Electronic and
another Vs. Addl
. Collector of Customs, A.P., reported
in 2006 (3) CTC 74, has observed that If such breaches of conditions
of warranty admittedly had taken place during the period of warranty, no
exception can be taken to the judgement and order passed by the Statement Commission
as also the National Commission. Further
observing that From the aforementioned conduct of the Appellant itself, it may be
inferred that it voluntarily undertook to meet the requirements of the
Respondent relating to mal-functioning, etc. of the said system despite expiry
of the period of warranty. For all
intent and purport, the period of warranty, thus, stood extended. As the defects in the system including
manufacturing defects, if any, were found not only during the period of
warranty but also during the extended period and as the Appellant itself
undertook to attend to the complaints received in that behalf, in our opinion,
it is too late, for it now to contend that in view of the fact that the period
of contract or warranty expired, it had not liability therefore. Thus, it is seen, if the mal-functioning of
the car or defect in the engine, had occurred during the warranty period, then
continued, not attended effectively, by the manufacturer or the service
provider undertaking to rectify the mistake, then it could be held that the
warranty period stood extended, not otherwise.
In this decision also,
Section 12
of Sale of Goods of Act was
considered, where, Condition and Warranty are available. Considering 12 (3) of that Section, in Para 28
of the judgement, it is stated Although
in terms of sub-section (3) of
Section 12
, no right accrues to a purchaser to
reject the goods on breach of stipulation of warranty, the same would not mean
that the extent of damages cannot be equivalent to the price of the goods in as
much as such a power has specifically been conferred upon the Commission, further
observing it is true, where a stipulation in a contract of sale is a warranty,
its breach may give rise to a claim for damages but not to a right to reject
the goods and treat the contract as repudiated; but, where a stipulation in a
contract of sale is a condition, its breach may give rise not only to a claim
for damages but also generally to a right to treat the contract as repudiated.
23. In M/s. Hyundai Motors India Ltd., Vs.
M/s.Hyundai Motors India Ltd., & Another, the National Commission had an occasion to consider the manufacturing
defect, and the conduct of Multi-National Company, manufacturing a car having
defects. As seen from the facts of the
case, within the period of one year, from the date of purchase of the vehicle,
fuel leaking occurred, white smoke reported, followed by running repair,
wherein, within the period of warranty, engine was dismantled, head assembly
repaired, and in this view, a direction came to be issued, to repay the entire
cost, in addition to, compensation and this decision will not come to the aid
of the complainant which period has run from the date of purchase exceeding the
warranty period also. Based upon
the
above decision
, the facts of the case should be seen.
24. The warranty period in
this case come to an end on 5.6.2001.
Therefore, we have to see within the period of warranty, whether the
complainant had complained any defect in the engine, in order to say, that
existed even during the period of warranty, so as to apply the dictum of the
Supreme Court ruling extending the period of warranty. As rightly submitted by the appellants,
during the period of warranty, for one year, there was no complaint of any
problem in the engine, whether it is jerking or abnormal noise as the case may
be and as seen from the repair order dated 6.7.2001 alone, the
Customer/Complainant complained about the vehicle jerking, and abnormal noise,
which was repaired as seen from the document dated 7.7.2001 (Ex.A4). Further,
as seen from the vehicle repair history, engine and other problems reported,
only after the period of warranty.
25. The learned senior counsel
submitted that the defect was admitted by the opposite parties, also not acceptable
to us, since the letter dated 17.1.2005, is not clear, regarding the defect
therein as if that had occurred during the period of warranty, as seen from
Para 2 of the letter dated 17.1.2005. Only after the vehicle run more than 20,000
kms, the complainant had raised the engine vibration, at idling and this defect
alone is stated in the notice, however.
Since the engine head was opened for repairing the defect, your client demanded
that 70% of the cost of repair be borne by the dealer that does not mean, that the defect was
admitted from the day one of the purchase, or within the period of
warranty. Therefore, on the basis of the
so called admission, it is not possible, for us to conclude that the defect was
admitted, that too, within the period of warranty, which should be construed as
extended, thereby, compelling the manufacturer, to replace the vehicle.
26. The perusal of the records
filed on behalf of the complainant, would disclose that jerking or vibration was
reported only after the period of warranty and therefore, the Forum cannot
compel the opposite parties, to replace the engine since the problem might have
occurred for some other reasons, certainly not because of manufacturing defect
or defect which had occurred within the period of warranty. As per the condition and warranty, if at all,
the complainant can claim damages, if deficiency in service is proved and he
cannot reject the goods asking for new one, which is prohibited. Here also, as and when reported, repairs were
rectified, and the complainant not satisfied, finally left the vehicle with the
second opposite party, for which, they cannot be held responsible, since they
have reported, that the vehicle is ready after repair, asking the complainant
to take delivery. Probably, to avoid the
expenses, and when there was dispute in sharing the cost of the repair, it
seems, the complainant left the vehicle, and approached the Forum, after 4
years and in this view, we find no deficiency in service, which was not properly,
considered by the District Forum. For
the foregoing reasons, we conclude, that the complainant is neither entitled to
replacement nor compensation, and the appeal deserves acceptance.
27. In
the result, both the appeals are allowed, setting aside the order of the
District Forum in O.P.213/2005, dated 31.07.2006 and the complaint is
dismissed.
28. However,
taking into consideration, that even after the warranty period, first and
second opposite parties have undertaken to repair the vehicle in question, they
are directed to repair the vehicle at free of cost as special case and hand
over the same to the complainant, issuing notice within two months, from this
date. There will be no order as to cost, in both the appeals.
PON
GUNASEKARAN M.
